reasons.mode: A flow, as the operator is dogfooding builds.

design:
TIER 1. No migration and no Hub-restart hazard. The live-app reach is the UI bundle commit (:8000 serves the committed bundle on reload), so the bundle is committed only with a passing drive.

DECISIONS
D1 (operator, 2026-11-08). The Hub classifies. A new module (hub/hub/operator_notices.py) holds the rules now in hub/ui/src/lib/notify/classify.ts, moved, not copied. It runs at the one broadcast seam (hub/hub/sse.py) and publishes an `operator_notice` event beside the original. The page's notifier stops classifying and renders notices. Non-blocking questions are ask, as the page does today: classify.ts never reads `blocking`.
D2 (operator, 2026-11-08). Windows choices per kind live in the Hub, instance-wide, in a small file in the Hub's profile data directory behind an operator-only GET/PUT route. That is no migration. The in-app per-kind switches stay as they are.
D3. The Windows notification is shown by the launcher side, never by the Hub, which stays platform-neutral and Docker-safe. With a window open, the page passes a notice to the bridge when the window is not in front. With the window closed and the Hub kept running, a hidden watcher run by the launcher (pythonw, one per port) reads the operator stream (/api/v1/events, ticket from /api/v1/events/ticket, credential as cli.py:1243 already obtains it). It ends when the Hub ends or a window opens. Both paths call the same notifier, which de-duplicates by notice id through a small per-port ledger, so the hand-over can overlap safely.
D4 (operator, 2026-11-08). The notification is shown by powershell.exe (Windows PowerShell 5.1, named explicitly, CREATE_NO_WINDOW as at cli.py:758) through Windows' own toast interface, so the CLI stays stdlib-only. A Start-menu shortcut carrying AppUserModelID AgentWeave.Hub (desktop_window.APP_ID) gives it the name and icon. The shortcut is created once and idempotently, beside the desktop one (cli.py:1076-1087). This is how Electron apps (Slack, VS Code) get attributed.
D5 (operator, 2026-11-08, option A). A click uses protocol activation. An `agentweave:` link is registered per user under HKCU\Software\Classes with winreg (stdlib), and the toast's launch is that link carrying port, project and conversation. The handler starts the launcher with an open target: it focuses the one window and tells the page to navigate (new `aw-app-open` window event beside the existing `aw-app-focus`, cli.py:1614), or opens a window on the running Hub without restarting it. The launcher-notify task tries this first. If Windows will not activate an unpackaged app this way, the builder calls report_cannot_satisfy on c-click; the fallback is that a click only brings AgentWeave to the front.
D6. question_asked gains conversation_id. The broadcast and persisted payloads are built once and are identical. The project is not added: the operator stream already stamps it.

CONTRACT
- operator_notice: {id, kind: ask|fail|done|reply, project_id, agent, conversation_id|null, title, text, source_event}.
- Bridge: notify(notice) -> bool (false when refused; never raises), called only when foreground() is false.
- Hub route for the Windows kinds: {ask, fail, done, reply} booleans.
- Off Windows, notifier calls return false and do nothing.
- AW_TOAST_COMMAND replaces the PowerShell call, for drives (recorder) and the quiet-failure test (failing command).

CURRENT: Hub event -> page classifies -> in-app toast. Window closed -> nothing.
PROPOSED: Hub event -> Hub notice -> page toast, and (window not in front or closed) -> notifier -> Windows notification -> click -> agentweave: link -> window at the conversation.

open_questions.question: Which kinds reach Windows? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): the operator chooses per kind in App settings; defaults question and failure on, done and reply off.
Do non-blocking questions reach Windows? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): yes, as the in-app notifier does today.
Second copy of the rules, or a Hub-made notice? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): the Hub sends one ready-made notice.
A background watcher while the window is closed? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): yes, a plain watcher now; a tray icon is a follow-up.

Add a notification package to the CLI? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): no; PowerShell with a Start-menu shortcut and a registered agentweave: link. If that cannot work, report it rather than add a package.
Click activation? Answered (operator, 2026-11-08): option A, try real activation first; report_cannot_satisfy if impossible, falling back to bringing AgentWeave to the front.

problem:
Calls for the operator live only in the page, so they vanish whenever the page is not in view.
- The page classifies Hub events into ask, fail, done and reply and plays the sound, shows an in-app toast, sets a title count and flashes the taskbar (hub/ui/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts; hub/ui/src/lib/notify/classify.ts). Nothing reaches Windows' own notifications.
- Closing the window can leave the Hub working: with work running the close asks stop / keep running / cancel, and a 'keep running' setting skips the question (src/agentweave/cli.py:1286-1350). With no page, nothing calls the operator at all, which is exactly when an agent waiting on them is easiest to miss.
- The classification rules exist only in the page, and the operator's switches live in the window's page storage (hub/ui/src/lib/notify/prefs.ts), so nothing without a window can apply either.
- A click cannot open the question's conversation: the question_asked event carries only id, from_agent and blocking (hub/hub/api/v1/questions.py:374-383), though the stored question has a conversation.
- Windows attributes a notification to an app only if the app has a registered identity (a Start-menu shortcut carrying its AppUserModelID). Slice 1 deferred that shortcut to this slice.

requirements.rationale: The operator chose (2026-11-08) one Hub-made notice over a second copy of the rules: the review already found the design's copied rule table disagreeing with the page on blocking questions, so a copy drifts.
requirements.statement: For every Hub event the in-app notifier treats today as ask, fail, done or reply (non-blocking questions included, as ask), the Hub SHALL publish exactly one notice on the operator stream carrying a stable notice id, its kind, project, agent, conversation when known, and the title and text the in-app toast shows; for every event it treats as silent, none. The in-app toast and any Windows notification for that event SHALL both be drawn from this notice.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-08: the operator selects which events reach Windows. The Hub holds it because the closed-window case has no page to read it from.
requirements.statement: App settings SHALL let the operator turn each kind (question, failure, done, reply) on or off for Windows notifications, separately from the in-app switches. The defaults SHALL be question and failure on, done and reply off. The choice SHALL be held by the Hub, apply while no window is open, and survive a Hub restart.

requirements.rationale: The in-app toast, sound and flash are not seen from another app.
requirements.statement: While the app window is open but not the foreground window (minimized or covered), each notice of a kind switched on for Windows SHALL appear as one Windows notification within 5 seconds of the notice.

requirements.rationale: Closing to the background currently silences the app entirely.
requirements.statement: While no app window is open and a Hub this launcher started is running, the same notices SHALL appear as Windows notifications within 5 seconds, with no console window shown at any point.

requirements.rationale: The in-app toast covers a window in front; the hand-over between window and background watcher must not duplicate or drop.
requirements.statement: While the app window is the foreground window, no Windows notification SHALL appear. No notice SHALL produce more than one Windows notification, including across the moment the window closes or reopens.

requirements.rationale: An unnamed or 'Windows PowerShell' notification cannot be told from anything else.
requirements.statement: A Windows notification SHALL show AgentWeave's name and icon as its source, and say which agent or project needs the operator and why, in the words of the in-app toast.

requirements.rationale: A notification that opens the app in the wrong place is a second hunt. Operator, 2026-11-08 (option A): try real click activation first; if it proves impossible, the builder reports the criterion as not satisfiable and the operator decides, rather than shipping a click that only appears to work.
requirements.statement: Clicking a notification SHALL bring the single AgentWeave window to the front, restored if minimized, on the project and conversation of its notice (the project overview for a permission request or a notice with no conversation). With no window open it SHALL open one on the running Hub without restarting it, so running work continues.

requirements.rationale: Without it, a question's notice can reach no further than the project.
requirements.statement: The question_asked event SHALL carry the id of the conversation the question belongs to (null when it has none); consumers that ignore the extra field SHALL behave as before.

requirements.rationale: A notification is a convenience, never a dependency for work.
requirements.statement: When Windows cannot show a notification (notifications off, focus assist, the shell call failing, not Windows), the app MUST carry on as before: the in-app toast, sound and flash still happen, and no error reaches the operator or interrupts any run.

in_scope: One Hub-made notice per event that calls the operator, used by both the in-app toast and Windows notifications.
The operator's choice per kind (question, failure, done, reply) of what reaches Windows, held by the Hub so it applies with the window closed.
A Windows notification when the window is not in front, or closed with the Hub running.
AgentWeave's name and icon on it, through a Start-menu shortcut.
A click opening AgentWeave at the conversation (project overview for a permission request), opening the window if none is open.
The question event carrying its conversation.
non_goals: A tray icon: a follow-up, once the plain watcher has been used (operator, 2026-11-08).
Adding a Python package to the CLI for notifications: if the PowerShell route cannot attribute or activate a notification, that is reported to the operator, not worked around (operator, 2026-11-08).
Notifications when the Hub itself is not running.
Action buttons or reply fields inside the notification.
macOS and Linux (the notifier does nothing there).
Docker-mode or remote Hubs: Windows notifications come only from a Hub this launcher started on this machine.

summary: Slice 4 of 'AgentWeave feels like a desktop app'. The Hub decides once which of its events call the operator and publishes one ready-made notice for each. The in-app toast and a new Windows notification both come from that notice. The operator chooses in App settings which kinds (question, failure, done, reply) reach Windows; by default questions and failures do. A notification shows AgentWeave's name and icon, appears when the window is not in front or is closed with the Hub still running, and a click opens AgentWeave at the conversation that asked.
